info.name: School ERP - Auth
info.description:
Endpoints from backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts. All routes live under the /api prefix.

Flow: run "Login" first (or "Login - Seeded SUPER_ADMIN") — it saves the access token into the {{accessToken}} collection variable and stores the httpOnly refresh cookie automatically via Postman's cookie jar (scoped to /api/auth, sameSite=lax). Every other request in this collection inherits Bearer auth from the collection level using {{accessToken}}.

Note: a freshly seeded or freshly admitted/reset login always has mustChangePassword: true in the response body — the real app forces a change-password screen before anything else. POST /auth/login and POST /auth/refresh return the current value of that flag on every call.

request.description: Public. Body: LoginDto { email, password }. Sets an httpOnly refresh_token cookie (scoped to /api/auth) and returns { accessToken, user }. user.mustChangePassword tells you whether this login must go through POST /auth/change-password before doing anything else in the real app.

Public, but requires the refresh_token httpOnly cookie set by Login (Postman's cookie jar sends it automatically for requests to this host). Rotates the refresh token and returns a new { accessToken, user }. 401 if no cookie was sent or the stored token was already rotated/revoked.

Requires Bearer {{accessToken}} (set by Login/Refresh). Returns the same AuthenticatedUserView shape as login/refresh: id, email, name, role, permissions, mustChangePassword, and student (only when role is STUDENT).

Requires Bearer {{accessToken}}. Body: ChangePasswordDto { currentPassword, newPassword (min 8 chars, must differ from current) }. Serves both the forced first-login change and a later voluntary change from Settings — same endpoint either way. On success, sets mustChangePassword to false and returns { user }. Does NOT issue new tokens.

401 if currentPassword is wrong. 400 if newPassword is under 8 characters or identical to currentPassword.

Heads up: running this against the seeded SUPER_ADMIN will actually change its password away from ChangeMe123! — point {{email}}/{{password}} at a disposable test account first if you just want to exercise this endpoint.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 or a validation/auth error', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400, 401]));

request.description: Requires Bearer {{accessToken}}. Clears the caller's stored hashedRefreshToken server-side (revokes it) and clears the refresh_token cookie. Returns 204 with no body.
